newsitem.title: GERMANY: Siemens transport unit may show 96/97 loss.
newsitem.headline: Siemens transport unit may show 96/97 loss.

text.p: German electronics and engineering giant Siemens AG said its transportation division may show a loss in 1996/97 as a result of the industry's worldwide consolidation and price cutting.

"Whether we can reach the break-even point remains to be seen," chief executive Heinrich von Pierer told the company's annual news conference. "Prices are not stable in this sector because of competition."
The price of an electric locomotive has fallen about 50 percent in the last five years to about five million marks, as the industry has consolidated, Von Pierer said.
Siemens is the world's third largest rail systems supplier behind ADtranz, a venture between Daimler-Benz AG and Swiss-Swedish engineering company ABB, and the French-British venture GEC Alsthom.
After a loss-making year in 1994/95, Siemens' transportation systems division showed a 19 million mark pretax profit in 1995/96. But it is still in restructuring to reduce costs.
In 1996/97 the group will have to carry start up costs for some rail projects in Asia, putting downward pressure on results, Pierer said.
Siemens expected a rebound in the group's results in 1997/98 when it completes those projects.
"We bill our customers when a project is completed, so we expect a clear improvement when these Asian contracts are paid," he said.
Although Siemens is looking to get out of unprofitable businesses, transportation would not become a potential target for divestment.
"This is a market that will continue to grow considerably, with trains, trams and railways expanding," he said. "Based on our technology, we are in a good position."
